toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.methodChoice: Kepner-Tregoe specification (IS/IS NOT by tenure band), then ACH across H1-H5, with evidence-ledger provenance check on the COO's claim.
output.brief:
The remote promotion gap is mostly a tenure effect, not proof of proximity bias. Remote hiring only opened widely in July 2024, so most remote staff are new. Only 32% of remote employees had the 18 months in level that policy requires to be nominated, against 74% of office staff. Among eligible people, rates are nearly the same: 20.0% remote and 21.1% office. Nomination rates (28%) and approval rates (71% vs 74%) are also close. Remote attrition is no higher than office attrition, and the job-family mix does not explain the gap. The dashboard's raw rate divides by everyone, so it compares unlike groups.

Caveat: only 110 remote employees are eligible, so a real gap of a few points could still exist. The manager interviews hint that urgent work goes to nearby staff, and I found no direct data on stretch assignments. Proximity bias is therefore not ruled out, only unproven.

Do not announce the three-day office rule. It would bar about 180 remote staff hired on home-based contracts, and the evidence doesn't support it. Instead, change the reporting to compare eligible employees only, and re-check at FY2027. Look at assignment staffing data separately.
